declared: 2026-09-17, committed and pushed before the declared procedure runs
question: at lambda 0.65625, do the fresh, lambda-0-history and lambda-1-history trajectories converge to one stationary band-valid late regime (slow convergence), settle into different stationary regimes (multistability), or keep drifting or switching (nonstationary)?

frozen.model: V2.1 static column, kernel baseline, HDP detached, no intrinsic heterogeneity, all-zero schedule, no shot noise, native noise default, jaxfne 0.4.24, dt 0.1 ms

initial_states.lambda_0_end_state: final ContinuationState of a 4 x 5 s fresh run at lambda 0 (engine key and step index continue)
initial_states.lambda_1_end_state: final ContinuationState of a 4 x 5 s fresh run at lambda 1
initial_states.note: identical to the sealed coupled-background runs; the 20 s pre-runs are recomputed, not loaded

procedure.S0_freeze: no parameter, tonic, noise, kernel or schedule change
procedure.S1_runs: for each initial state, 12 x 5 s (60 s) at lambda 0.65625. Chunk 0 is settling (existing convention); windows 1-11 are the recorded trajectory
procedure.S1_reproduction: windows 1-3 of each trajectory must match the sealed 20 s runs (results/v21_coupled_background.json: candidate fresh run and the two hysteresis runs) within 0.5 Hz per class per window
procedure.S2_record: per window 1-11 and per initial state: class rates E, PV, SST, VIP (operation.window_summary); active fraction and sync recorded, not gating
procedure.S2_late_stationary: prospective_v2 check drift (the existing V2 criterion, (max - min) / mean <= 0.2 for every class) evaluated on windows 9-11
procedure.S2_same_regime: for every pair of initial states and every class, |late mean difference| <= max(1 Hz, 0.1 * fresh late mean) (the sealed state-dependence tolerance, applied to windows 9-11)
procedure.S2_reversal: PV trajectory over windows 1-11 reverses direction: some window lies above (or below) at least one earlier and one later window by more than max(1 Hz, 0.1 * mean PV rate of that trajectory)

classification.2: if every trajectory is late-stationary: PV_MULTISTABILITY if S2_same_regime fails; PV_STATIONARITY_PASS if the regime is shared and band-valid for every trajectory; otherwise PV_STATIONARITY_UNRESOLVED (a shared stationary regime that fails the bands, a case outside the reviewer's four labels, flagged in the reason)
classification.3: PV_NONSTATIONARY if some trajectory is not late-stationary and at least one such trajectory shows a PV reversal
classification.4: PV_STATIONARITY_UNRESOLVED otherwise (late drift with a monotone PV trajectory: slow convergence not excluded within 60 s)

consequence_declared_by_reviewer: PASS: the coupled-background result may be upgraded to COUPLED_BACKGROUND_PASS at lambda 0.65625 by the reviewer, and closed-network susceptibility becomes the next task. MULTISTABILITY or NONSTATIONARY: stop the background program. This lineage does not rewrite results/v21_coupled_background.json
limits: one noise realization per initial state; 'reproducibly different' in PV_MULTISTABILITY means stationary over windows 9-11 of that realization, not across seeds
forbidden: parameter, tonic, noise or schedule changes
ISI-CV, synchrony or heterogeneity as criteria
pre_seal_disclosure: no simulation for this lineage before this spec; the classifier was exercised on synthetic trajectories only (test_classify_known_cases)
